asr: meeting is in new yolk sity tomorrow
expected_formatted: Meeting is in new yolk sity tomorrow.
expected_memory_aware: Meeting is in New York City tomorrow.
notes: Two-token observed span ('yolk sity') matched and replaced with a two-token canonical form ('York City'), demonstrating multi-word memory entries beyond the brief's single-word example. 'new' -> 'New' is a separate, single-token mid-sentence recasing memory (same mechanism as brief_example_001's 'sarvam'); the diff can't tell it's part of the same proper noun without real entity extraction (documented follow-up work), but applying both still reconstructs 'New York City' correctly.

Known limitation, deliberately documented: multi-word spans only match by exact normalized text (no fuzzy tolerance implemented for span_len > 1), so 'york city' (already correctly spelled here, just lowercase) doesn't match the 'yolk sity' memory and stays untouched. The single-token 'new' -> 'New' memory matches independently and does apply, producing a partially-corrected, admittedly inconsistent-looking result - a known limitation of word-level (not phrase-level) memory, not a bug.

Two competing corrections both reach 'active' with equal confidence (2 observations each); the more recently reinforced one ('Adithya') wins the tie-break, and the explanation flags that multiple candidates existed.
'adithya' is a 1-edit-distance ASR typo of the learned 'aditya' - within the fuzzy-match budget for a 6-letter word, so it still resolves correctly.
'rajesh' is far too different from 'aditya' (well beyond the edit-distance budget) - must NOT fuzzy-match; negative control against overly aggressive fuzzy matching.

Short words (<=4 letters) get zero fuzzy-match tolerance by design - too easy to false-positive on unrelated short words - so 'naya' does not fuzzy-match the learned 'nayha' even though they are only 1 edit apart.
